sections.html:
A Lawrenceville owner can list with an agent, sell without one, or accept an as-is offer. The condition of the house and your move-out date usually settle the question. A tidy house with updated systems tends to draw several showings through an agent. A property with deferred repairs or a clouded title may close faster with a buyer who pays cash, since that buyer does not need a lender's appraisal.

Whichever route you take, line up the deed, your latest city and county tax bills, and any permit paperwork before the first offer arrives. Having those on hand shortens every route.

Lawrenceville is the seat of Gwinnett County, around 30 miles northeast of downtown Atlanta, with about 32,822 residents in the 2025 estimate. Gwinnett is among Georgia's busiest property markets. Typical owner-occupied value runs $350,600, typical gross rent is $1,613, and 47.0 percent of the city's 10,719 households own their home.

More than four in ten residents speak another language at home, so a listing that reaches buyers in several languages can pull in people an English-only ad would miss. If your house is a short walk from the historic square, with its arts center, lawn and trails, lead the listing with that. Long commutes are common here, so buyers also weigh access to State Route 316, U.S. 78 and U.S. 29.

Since tax year 2021 the city has billed its own property tax, so a Lawrenceville seller sees two bills: Gwinnett County's and the City Finance Department's. The city's 2026 millage rate is 3.26 mills, and each mill means one dollar of tax per thousand of assessed value. Assessed value is 40 percent of the fair market value set by the Gwinnett Board of Assessors.

The Finance Department can tell you the due date at 678-407-6675. Have the closing attorney check both bills before the sale, so the buyer sees that each one was settled.

sections.h2: Due dates, penalties and the city homestead credit
sections.html:
City residents with a homestead get $20,000 off assessed value, except on debt service levies. Late bills draw monthly interest at the prime rate plus 3 percent, and a 5 percent penalty is added every 120 days until it reaches 20 percent.

Lawrenceville city tax at a glance
Charge or ruleWhat applies
Who bills the city taxThe city itself, starting with tax year 2021
2026 city millage3.26 mills
City basic homestead$20,000 off assessed value
Late charges5 percent per 120 days, up to 20 percent of principal
NonpaymentFiFa (lien) under O.C.G.A. 48-3-3

The Gwinnett Tax Commissioner takes applications until April 1, and the house must have been your primary residence on January 1 of that year. Nothing is granted automatically, and once granted an exemption does not need to be renewed. You can apply online at GwinnettTaxCommissioner.com/apply.

A sale ends your exemption. The buyer applies separately for their own.

A house with unpaid city or county tax can usually still be sold. The balance comes out of your proceeds at closing. Georgia law lets the taxing office file a FiFa lien on unpaid tax, so it is wiser to settle the balance before you accept an offer than to let a lien surface during title review. Ask Finance for a payoff figure and hand it to the closing attorney. Do the same with the Gwinnett Tax Commissioner for the county bill, since the two offices keep separate accounts and a buyer's title company will look at both.

If you inherited the house or a tenant lives in it, tell every buyer up front. Surprises found after an offer is accepted are the usual reason a closing slips.

Planning and Development issues permits through the Licensing, Permits and Plans portal, and registering there costs nothing. Electrical, mechanical, plumbing, occupancy and structural jobs each call for a building permit. A Certificate of Occupancy must come first when a building's use changes.

Permits go only to a buildable lot of record, meaning land recorded in Gwinnett's court records before June 2, 1970, or shown on an approved, recorded plat. Sewer, water and septic permits are issued by Gwinnett County. Planning and Development, at 678-407-6583, can tell you about any open permit.

  • Pull the permit history for the address from Planning and Development.
  • Keep Certificate of Occupancy paperwork for any addition.
  • Ask Gwinnett County for sewer, water or septic permit records if work touched those systems.

Open permits can hold up a buyer's loan or title review, so confirm that old jobs were closed. A sale itself does not trigger a permit.

Expect a buyer's inspector to look at drainage around the foundation, gutter condition and attic ventilation first. Fix a clogged downspout or a soft spot in the grading before listing and you remove an easy negotiating point.

The city's tax bill can also carry a stormwater fee. It pays for drainage structures the city maintains and is separate from the county water bill. Check that line so a buyer sees the full yearly cost of owning the property.

The historic square anchors the city. The Lawrenceville Arts Center, home of the Aurora Theatre, draws about 80,000 visitors a year. The Lawrenceville Lawn has an amphitheater, dog park and walking path, and Rhodes Jordan Park covers 162 acres with a fishing lake, swim facilities and a 1.9-mile paved trail. Freeman's Grist Mill, a county park with a trail and picnic pavilion, sits inside the city.

Schools come from Gwinnett County Public Schools, and zoning follows the street address. Some Lawrenceville addresses are zoned to schools outside the city limits, so ask the district to confirm the assignment before you name a school in the listing. Buyers with children will check.

Streets near the square look quite different from newer subdivisions, so tell buyers which era your house belongs to and price it against its own neighbors.

1. Collect the deed, both tax bills and permit records.
  2. Compare offers by what you net, not just the headline price.
  3. Ask the closing attorney to confirm how the city and county bills will be handled in the contract.
  4. Clear any open permit or lien before the title search.
  5. Tell the Tax Commissioner the house changed hands, because your exemption ends at the sale.

A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and repair requests, which is why it suits a house that would struggle to qualify for a mortgage.

faqs.q: Does the City of Lawrenceville send its own tax bill?
faqs.a: Yes, since tax year 2021. The Gwinnett County bill no longer includes the city tax, and Finance answers questions at 678-407-6675.

faqs.q: What is the city's 2026 millage rate?
faqs.a: It is 3.26 mills, or $3.26 for each $1,000 of assessed value. That covers the city levy only, not county or school taxes.

faqs.q: What is the last day to apply for a Gwinnett homestead exemption?
faqs.a: April 1. You must have owned and lived in the house on January 1, and an approved exemption stays in place without yearly reapplication.

faqs.q: Can a house with unpaid city tax still be sold?
faqs.a: Usually, with the balance taken from proceeds at closing. Georgia law allows a FiFa lien on unpaid tax, so settle it before accepting an offer.

faqs.q: Must I get a permit before selling?
faqs.a: No permit is needed just to sell. Open permits can still delay a buyer's loan or title review, so confirm with Planning and Development that old jobs were closed.
